subject: Operator access windows and BYOK audit procedures for private deployment

Subject: BYOK operator access / audit window question for private deploy

Hi Aditya / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. One of the outstanding items from our compliance team: we need a concrete description of (1) the typical operator "access window" during BYOK key onboarding and (2) the audit evidence you can provide proving access was limited to those windows. We have an internal requirement that any operator intervention that touches our customer-managed keys must be logged and contain an approval artefact; we also need to understand how long Redwood retains those logs and any forensic snapshots.

Specific asks:
- What triggers operator access for a private (on-prem) BYOK provisioning?
- How long will operator sessions be allowed (maximum window) and do you support timeboxed breakglass?
- What artifacts/logs will you produce for our auditors and in what format?
- Do any subprocessors ever see key material or unencrypted data during onboarding? If so, who and where?

We appreciate a short timeline for the onboarding day so we can align our security ops and procurement.

Mike
Security / IT Operations
HorizonHealth

Mike — thanks for the clear list. Putting answers below and attaching a short checklist (byok-audit-checklist-v2.pdf) we run with customers during private deploy onboarding. High level: we do not access customer key material in plaintext; operator actions are narrowly scoped and timeboxed; evidence packages are produced as encrypted archives and can be delivered to your secure collection point.

Quick answers:
- Triggers: operator access is only triggered by one of the following: (A) customer-scheduled key provisioning event (you open a ticket and nominate a time), (B) explicit mutual-action-plan step during troubleshooting logged in the onboarding MIP, or (C) emergency breakglass invoked by the customer. Operators do not perform unscheduled key imports.

- Windowing: standard window is 2 hours for planned provisioning; we enforce session timeboxing and automatic termination at window end. For complex migrations we allow a scheduled 4-hour window split into two 2-hour sessions with a mandatory change control entry between sessions. Breakglass sessions are 30 minutes by default and require immediate escalation with justification.

- Evidence and retention: we produce a signed evidence bundle per session that includes: session start/end timestamps, operator identity (SAML subject), ephemeral session token hash, request/response summaries, and a live-preserved audit log extract. Archives are delivered as PGP-encrypted tarballs and retained on Redwood for 90 days by default (extendable via contract). Logs include live command transcripts where applicable and automated KV-cache access markers.

- Subprocessors: during BYOK onboarding we do not disclose plaintext key material to subprocessors. We may use a managed remote-support provider (listed in the attached subprocessor roster) to coordinate infrastructure-level tasks (hardware provisioning, network cabling) but they never receive key material. If a subprocessor must access host-level storage for forensic capture, we do it under customer-directed escrow flow and with auditable remediation steps; this is rare and customer-approved per-case.

Next steps: I suggest a 30-min alignment call tomorrow where we walk through the checklist and agree session times. Kimberly and Neha are looped for legal and retention questions.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BYOK operator access / audit window question for private deploy

Mike — legal/contract side here. A few clarifications and a proposed contract addendum text below. Thanks for flagging retention and auditor artifacts; we can accommodate most of HorizonHealth's requirements but need to align on these points ahead of signing: 

1) Escrow / key custody statement: Redwood will not retain or escrow customer key material except when explicitly agreed (e.g., on-site escrow that Horizon requests and signs). If escrow is requested, we will include explicit custody handoff steps and require a dual-signer approval.

2) Subprocessors: the attached roster lists the small set of vendors we may engage. We will not permit subprocessors to access plaintext CMK. If Horizon requires subprocessor-specific attestations, we can provide SOC2 subprocessor evidence and targeted attestations under NDA.

3) Evidence format and chain-of-custody: our evidence bundle is intended for forensic review but we can provide additional hash chaining and notarization via a third-party timestamping service (can be added as an SOW line item).

4) Data exit / egress procedure: when a provisioning session is complete, any temporary snapshots or exported logs are wiped and a deletion certificate is provided. We propose a 7-day hold for egress evidence (so your auditors can request copies) and then automatic deletion. If Horizon requires a longer hold, include it as a contract variable.

Draft addendum bullets (short):
- Redwood will limit operator sessions to scheduled windows unless otherwise authorized by Horizon.
- All operator actions will be recorded and an evidence bundle delivered within 48 hours.
- Subprocessors will not have access to customer-managed key material.
- Temporary artifacts created during provisioning will be deleted and a deletion certificate issued within 7 days unless otherwise agreed.

If that looks acceptable, Aditya — please call out any technical caveats on the windowing and evidence packaging. Mike — happy to jump on the call as well if your legal team wants to be present.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
